solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Joint vote rigged in Irish parliamentary house

indicators.note: a rigged vote has been fixed or tampered with, so its letters are rearranged
the jumbled word sits inside the parliament named next

blocks.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament
taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A dodgy shared vote taking place in the Irish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a shared or political word, but it is the carpentry definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a woodworking joint of interlocking wedge-shaped tenons.

definitions.note: describes the mammoth: the prehistoric beast is called the woolly mammoth

blocks.note: first meaning: vague and confused in thought
second meaning: covered in thick hair, like the extinct elephant

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: the extinct beast is always called the woolly mammoth.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly describes confused, imprecise thinking and also a shaggy coat of thick hair.

clue.text: Animal burying first of presents in earth

indicators.note: to bury something is to put it inside, so the ground word wraps around the letter
only the opening letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: terrain is land or ground
initial letter of presents

explanation.surface: A creature hiding its gifts by digging them into the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, which is an animal.

indicators.note: the letters needed sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the tail of the first word joined to the head of the second

explanation.surface: Boasting that the dining room in one's house is luxurious.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the room where members of the armed forces eat together.

blocks.note: first meaning: an energetic, forceful person
second meaning: a machine turning motion into electric current

explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface of a live wire inside a generator hides that 'Live wire' means a lively person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is both an electrical generator and, figuratively, a person of tireless energy.

indicators.note: 'so to speak' style phrasing points to how the words are pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: something banned is not allowed

explanation.surface: Asking whether a group has been silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not allowed to speak' reads as a gag order, but 'to speak' is the sound signal applied to 'not allowed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group, whether of musicians or of people united by a cause.

blocks.note: a log is a written record
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A record of an ancient badge or symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a company's emblem or identifying symbol.

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are set out differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remarking that an ordinary citizen has a very odd name.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Public and Everyman both denote the ordinary, typical member of the public.

blocks.note: first meaning: informal word for a man, a variant of fella
second meaning: a person who cuts down trees

explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for a man; the question mark signals the playful second sense of one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Feller is colloquial for a man, and literally also a person who fells timber.

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
something handy is close by and easily reached

explanation.surface: A small drink kept close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' looks like a signal to put one thing inside another, but 'within reach' is a single phrase defining HANDY, which simply follows S. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a drink of beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: A piece of cake each — extremely scrummy

indicators.note: taking the extremes means keeping only the two end letters of the next word

blocks.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each
first and last letters of scrummy

explanation.surface: Handing out a slice of cake to everyone, and very tasty it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrummy is British slang for delicious. The definition is the idiom, not a literal slice.
explanation.definitionFit: 'A piece of cake' is an idiom for something simple to do, which is easy.

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning and turning things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like a nation, but it is the adjective, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life and scenery, the countryside as opposed to the town.

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and end up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer of the past sets the local butchers dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Schubert, the nineteenth-century Austrian composer, wrote over six hundred art songs (lieder).

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox: something terribly near yet distant out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' could be a container signal, but here it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco, from Italian 'in the fresh air', means taking place in the open air.

indicators.note: the letters needed lie inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Something in a chapel being even denser than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleventh is an ordinal number, giving position in a sequence rather than quantity.

blocks.note: first meaning: a male first name
second meaning: the winner of a contest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' in crosswords often signals a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor is a boy's name and also a word for a winner, who would be awarded first prize.

blocks.note: first meaning: a boiled suet dessert
second meaning: British slang for poor or useless

explanation.walkthrough: Plum duff is a traditional British steamed suet pudding with dried fruit; duff is also British slang for worthless or faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff names a heavy boiled dessert and, as slang adjective, means substandard or broken.

blocks.note: first meaning: abandon
second meaning: a hot, arid area of land

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently, de-SERT and DES-ert, though spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon someone, and a desert is a hot barren expanse like the Sahara.

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to discuss something is to talk about it

explanation.surface: A quick chat about an athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus throw is an athletics field event in which a heavy disc is hurled.

clue.text: Bird's heading off — a very short distance!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and off means it is removed

blocks.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird sets off but only travels a tiny way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' reads as setting out, but it means the bird's first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, used idiomatically for a tiny distance.

clue.text: Good numbers coming up — one of those?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
NOS is the abbreviation for numbers

explanation.surface: Pleasant numbers on the way, and asking whether this is one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those' refers back to 'numbers' in the musical sense: a song is a number. The question mark marks this cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical number is a song or piece in a performance, so a song is one such number.

blocks.note: first meaning: US slang form of address to a man
second meaning: one who busts or breaks things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen, buster' is American slang for addressing a man; the question mark covers the literal sense of one who busts things.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster is a US mode of address for a man, and literally a breaker or wrecker.

clue.text: Glass horse on front of cabinet broken

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept
something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
initial letter of cabinet

explanation.surface: A glass horse ornament on top of a cabinet has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a positional link, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a large tall drinking glass, used for sherry in Britain or beer in Australia.

blocks.note: first meaning: to move fast, especially against others
second meaning: a contest of speed

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single instruction, but splits into a verb and a noun sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to run at speed, and a race is a contest to see who is fastest.
